title: When the Letters Breaks
premise: Mara Whitlock ghostwrites memoirs for celebrities, and her newest client is Julian Voss—the estranged brother of the man she once loved and lost, Theo. When Theo's family reunion demands a plus-one, Mara agrees to pose as Julian's girlfriend to get close enough to finish the book, never expecting Theo himself to walk in after seven years abroad. Over one long weekend, old loyalties fracture as Mara realizes the memoir she's writing could destroy the family that once claimed her—and that Theo left because of a letter she never sent. In the end, she reads the decade-old letter aloud at the reunion's final dinner, choosing truth over safety, and Theo chooses her over the version of home he'd been mourning.
about_author: Paloma Lockridge is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's unsent letters before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Maine coast, where she lives with her partner and an opinionated cat named Marginalia.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Deep into ghostwriting Julian Voss's memoir, Mara discovers a chapter about 'the girl who broke my brother'—herself, unnamed. Panicked but needing the money and the access, she accepts Julian's desperate request: be his fake girlfriend at the family reunion so he can face his mother. The beat is dread braided with longing; Mara agrees knowing exactly whose house she'll walk into.

chapters.title: Dessert and Other Confessions
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with an interlude from Theo's journal entries woven between scenes. The reunion begins: Theo is there, seven years older and colder. Forced proximity over two days—shared kitchen duty, a rainstorm trapping them in the boathouse—cracks their armor. By dessert on night two, the fake date with Julian feels like betrayal while every glance at Theo feels like coming home. Beat: the past stops being past.

chapters.title: What the Letter Never Said
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Mara and Theo. Theo confronts Mara privately, accusing her of abandoning him a decade ago; she learns his departure was triggered by a misread letter she wrote but never sent. Meanwhile Julian discovers her manuscript notes revealing she's the ghostwriter—and the brother's ex. Loyalties detonate: Julian threatens exposure, Theo feels used twice. Beat: everything Mara built to stay safe collapses at once.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Spoken
chapters.summary: Mara's POV closing with Theo's answer. At the farewell dinner, with Julian poised to expose her, Mara stands and reads the unsent letter aloud—confessing her love, her silence, and her fear—to the whole family. The room holds its breath; Theo crosses the room before she finishes. Julian, disarmed by honesty rather than scandal, offers to publish the memoir under both their names. Beat: belonging chosen out loud, at last.
